question: A shipping warehouse had 140 pallets stacked, even though the warehouse has 60 loading docks. Seven more matching truckloads arrived, making the pallet count eight times as large. A big outbound shipment then removed 547 pallets. A regional hub sent four more matching truckloads, making the total five times as large. Another large shipment removed 560 pallets. Finally, a merger with a sister warehouse doubled the remaining pallet count. How many pallets were in the warehouse at the end?

An aquarium had 213 coral fragments growing in its main tank. A shipment to a partner aquarium removed 179 fragments. A propagation event, where four new tanks each grew matching fragments, made the count five times as large. A hobbyist then donated 18 more fragments. Finally, a breeding tank yielded 26 more fragments. How many coral fragments did the aquarium have in the end?

Nina had 82 dollars saved, even though her piggy bank has a dozen coin slots. She spent 59 dollars on a new backpack, out of the 20 styles the store carried. She then paid 9 dollars for a bus pass. A birthday gift from three relatives, each matching her remaining amount, made her total four times as large. Finally, she earned 7 more dollars from selling lemonade, ending up with more than her cousin Ella, who only had 30 dollars. How much money did Nina have at the end?

A charity clothing drive collected 205 jackets in the first week, even though the drive has a dozen collection points across town. A second week added 43 more jackets. A partnership with seven other drives, each matching the total exactly, made the count eight times as large. A late donation added 51 more jackets. A shipment of 829 jackets was sent out to a shelter downtown. Finally, six more matching partner drives joined, making the remaining count seven times as large. How many jackets were left with the charity?

Two rival shops compared inventories. Owen's shop had 168 umbrellas in stock, tracked over 240 minutes, or 4 hours, of a busy sale. A supplier's promotion, with seven matching shipments, made his stock eight times as large, even though the shop has a dozen display racks. One umbrella was returned as defective and removed. A late shipment added 79 more umbrellas. A final restock tripled his stock one more time. Owen's shop ended up with far more umbrellas than his rival Cade's shop, which only had 900. How many umbrellas did Owen's shop have at the end?

A tech recycling center had 142 old phones dropped off, even though the center accepts 15 different device types. Six partner centers each matched that count exactly, making the total seven times as large. A weekend drive added 35 more phones. A school fundraiser added 72 more. Finally, a citywide collection event made the total eight times as large. How many phones did the recycling center end up with?

Two food banks compared their canned goods. Riverside Food Bank had 195 cans, even though it has a dozen volunteers on staff. The cans were split evenly among 3 storage rooms, and only one room's cans were counted going forward. A shipment error meant 31 cans had to be discarded, out of the 500 cans donated citywide that month. A donation drive then added 62 more cans. A matching grant from five community partners made the room's count six times as large. Finally, 390 cans were sent out to shelters, leaving Riverside Food Bank well behind the rival Lakeside Food Bank's 700 cans. How many cans did Riverside Food Bank have left?

In the morning, a construction site had 190 bricks stacked, delivered after a 120-minute, or 2-hour, unloading process. By midday, 5 more bricks arrived on a small truck. In the afternoon, two more matching truckloads tripled the stack. By evening, three more matching truckloads made the stack four times as large. Finally, 23 more bricks were added from a leftover pile. How many bricks were stacked at the site by the end of the day?

Two rival bakeries compared their cupcake orders. Sweet Treats had 187 cupcakes ordered, priced at 18,700 cents in total, even though the shop offers 20 flavors. A wedding order added 37 more cupcakes. A birthday order added 47 more. A cancellation then removed 172 cupcakes from the total. Finally, a catering contract made the remaining order seven times as large, well ahead of the rival bakery's order of 400 cupcakes. How many cupcakes did Sweet Treats end up with in their order?

In the morning, a food pantry had 109 boxes of supplies. By midday, 11 more boxes arrived from a small donor. In the afternoon, a school drive added 62 more boxes. Later, a church group added 14 more. By evening, a corporate sponsor added 74 more boxes. Finally, a matching grant made the total three times as large. How many boxes did the food pantry have by the end of the day?

A rock band sold 57 concert t-shirts at their first show, even though the venue holds a dozen merchandise tables. The second show added 9 more sales. The third show added 30 more. The fourth show added 36 more. A fifth show added 28 more, out of the 500 tickets sold that night. Finally, a nationwide tour bonus made the total nine times as large. How many t-shirts had the band sold in total?

Two hikers compared their trail mix supplies. Jorge started with 125 grams of trail mix, even though his backpack has a dozen pockets. He ate 39 grams on the first leg of the hike. He shared 67 grams with a tired stranger on the trail. He then dropped and lost 15 grams crossing a stream. A fellow hiker gave him 74 grams to make up for it. Finally, he found 67 more grams in a cache left by his hiking club, ending up with more than his friend Lila, who only had 100 grams left. How many grams of trail mix did Jorge have at the end?

In the morning, a soup kitchen had 76 loaves of bread. By midday, 68 loaves had been given out to visitors. In the afternoon, the remaining loaves were split evenly between two shelves, and only one shelf's loaves were kept out. Later, two more matching batches were baked, tripling that shelf's count. By evening, 69 more loaves arrived from a bakery donation. Finally, a matching donation doubled the shelf's count once more. How many loaves were on that shelf by evening?

A used bookstore had 175 novels on the clearance table, even though the store carries 40 different genres. A big sale sold 77 of them. A donation pickup removed 25 more for a library sale. A restock event, with eight matching donation boxes, made the table's count nine times as large. Finally, a weekend sale sold 416 more books. How many novels were left on the clearance table?

A candle shop had 154 candles in stock, valued at 15,400 cents, even though the shop sells 30 different scents. Eight matching wholesale shipments arrived, making the stock nine times as large. Five more matching shipments then made it six times as large again. A big holiday order shipped out 2,905 candles. Finally, 19 more candles were added from a returned order. How many candles were left in the shop?

Two rival card shops compared their trading card stock. Prime Cards had 117 packs on the shelf. A small delivery added 10 more packs. A distributor deal, with three matching shipments, made the stock four times as large. A regional warehouse deal then made it eight times as large. A final merger doubled the stock once more, leaving Prime Cards with far more packs than its rival, Ace Cards, which only had 2,000. How many packs did Prime Cards end up with?

A vineyard harvested 165 crates of grapes in the first pick. Six neighboring vineyards each matched that harvest exactly, making the total seven times as large. A shipment to a spoiled batch removed 897 crates. A second round of six matching vineyards joined in, making the total seven times as large again. A co-op merger with two more equal partners made it three times as large. Finally, a regional festival order made the total five times as large. How many crates of grapes did the vineyard end up with?

In the morning, a beekeeper counted 41 jars of honey ready for sale. By midday, 3 more jars were filled from the last batch. In the afternoon, 32 jars were sold at the farmers market. Later, 71 more jars were filled from a fresh harvest. By evening, five other beekeepers pooled in matching batches, making the total six times as large. Finally, 73 more jars arrived from a late harvest. How many jars of honey did the beekeeper have by evening?

A toy factory produced 232 dolls in the first hour, working 60 minutes, or 1 hour, straight. Seven more matching production runs made the hour's total eight times as large. A second shift doubled that total. A weeklong campaign with eight more matching runs made it nine times as large. A quality-check batch added 32 more dolls. Finally, a holiday rush order made the total six times as large. How many dolls did the factory end up with?

A soccer team had 63 dollars in their equipment fund, saved from 120 minutes, or 2 hours, of a car wash fundraiser. A bake sale added 14 more dollars. A raffle added 52 more. The team spent 71 dollars on new jerseys. A parent donated 29 more dollars. Finally, the team spent 12 dollars on a first-aid kit. How much money was left in the fund?

Two rival garden clubs compared their tomato harvests. The Elm Street club picked 159 tomatoes, then split them evenly across 3 volunteer baskets, keeping only one basket for the count. Two more matching baskets were combined back in, tripling that basket's count. A late picking added 54 more tomatoes. Finally, four other clubs joined a co-op, making the total five times as large, well ahead of the rival Oak Street club's 400 tomatoes. How many tomatoes did the Elm Street club end up with?

Two brothers compared their marble collections. Diego had 35 marbles to start, even though the marble jar has 20 different colors. He won 14 more in a schoolyard game. A trading swap with eight friends, each matching his count, made his total nine times as large. He found 6 more marbles under his bed. A tournament with seven more matching players made his total eight times as large. A final swap with three more matching players made it four times as large. Finally, he was given 46 more marbles by his grandfather, ending up with far more than his brother Mateo, who only had 500. How many marbles did Diego end up with?

A used electronics store had 60 phone cases in a clearance bin, even though the store stocks 90 different phone models. A donation added 59 more cases. A second donation added 59 more. A supplier delivered 37 more cases. Finally, a big weekend sale sold 175 cases. How many cases were left in the bin?

A school choir had 15 members at the start of the year, rehearsing for 90 minutes, or 1.5 hours, each week, even though the music room holds a dozen chairs. Five more matching sections joined, making the choir six times as large. Three more matching sections then joined, making it four times as large again. A scheduling conflict caused 290 members to drop out before the concert. A late sign-up added 3 more members. Finally, 10 more joined after a recruitment drive. How many members were in the choir at the end?

In the morning, a moving crew had 216 boxes to load, budgeted for 240 minutes, or 4 hours, of work. By midday, 78 more boxes were added from a second household. In the afternoon, 45 more boxes came from a storage unit, even though the truck has 12 tie-down straps. Later, six more matching truckloads joined the delivery run, making the total seven times as large. By evening, 593 boxes were delivered to the destination. How many boxes were left on the trucks by evening?
